findings.reason: the plan must either migrate _section_response's section text onto section_prose, as it does for dispatch._plan_section_text, or add a one-line reason that reader stays, since otherwise its stated single-owner goal is not met and the reader can diverge from the digest's prose.
findings.text: §16 makes section_prose "the one reader of a plan's authored text" and migrates dispatch._plan_section_text onto it, but the same module it rewrites, mcp_views, carries a second one-section text reader in _section_response whose line 2238 builds a section's text with its own BeautifulSoup(...).stripped_strings walk; the plan's prior-art claim ("the package already carries two readers") is checked against the code and is incomplete, so the drift §16 exists to prevent survives in the module it edits

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — section_prose on reckon/_plan_html.py hides span slicing, machinery-skip, entity decoding and whitespace collapse behind one function that three consumers across two packages read, and _section_digests digests its values rather than re-walking.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: pass — §16 converges prose onto one reader and the coverage question onto one predicate, deleting the gate's read_plan_review and the sweep's _plan_review_pending reader rather than sitting beside them, and names evidence._section_key, ledger.normalize_section and promotion._plan_remaining_sections with the reason each stays.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 1480, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §16 adds one public definition (section_prose, 1480→1481) and states nothing is retired at the counted level with the reason the identity digest and prose walk keep their names, adds no refusal family by reusing plan-review-missing, and §20 adds none.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §16 names two readers of a plan's authored text (mcp_views.authored_plan_text, dispatch._plan_section_text) and makes section_prose "the one reader", but mcp_views._section_response extracts a section's visible text with its own BeautifulSoup walk at reckon/mcp_views.py:2238, unaccounted for.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the coverage predicate is one function over two existing public readers (roadmap.implementable_sections, list_plan_reviews) and the plan argues why it is not a wrapper of read_plan_review; _strip_tags reuses the existing _TAG_RE and the plan states why count_open_decisions keeps its own bare substitution.
